rows.heading: 1.1 Purpose > Purpose > 1.1
rows.section_text:
1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of OT Malicious Code Prevention procedure is to provide a process to document the use 
of malicious code prevention methods to deter, detect, prevent, and mitigate the threat of detected 
malicious code, as well as establish a process to update malware signatures.

rows.heading: 3.5 CMLAP Log Review for CIP High Impact BES Cyber Systems, EACM, and PCA Devices > CMLAP Log Review for CIP High Impact BES Cyber Systems, EACM, and PCA Devices > 3.5
rows.section_text:
3.5 CMLAP Log Review for CIP High Impact BES Cyber Systems, EACM, and PCA Devices 
3.5.1 
For CIP Cyber Assets where logs are maintained by a CMLAP: 
3.5.1.1 
OT shall review a summarization or sampling of logged events for Applicable Systems, at 
a minimum at intervals no greater than fifteen (15) calendar days, to identify undetected 
Cyber Security Incidents. 
• 
Completion of this review shall be documented in a Compliance Tracking Tool task. 
• 
OT will escalate all potential cybersecurity incidents to OT Security Management. 
3.5.2 For CIP Cyber Assets, where logs are not maintained by a CMLAP with automated alerting 
capability, OT shall review these logs, as close to daily as possible, to detect any real or 
suspected Cyber Security Incidents. 
3.5.2.1 
Log review shall be documented and performed, as described in  Appendix 2: Steps for 
Manual Log Review 
3.5.3 All Cyber Security Incidents that are identified by a log review shall trigger execution of OT 
Security Incident Response Procedure by either the OT Security Operations or OT Security & 
Compliance team upon notification or the reviewing entity. 
3.5.4 Upon discovery of a real or suspected reportable Cyber Security

CIP-004 R5 – Access Revocation 
R5. Each Responsible Entity shall implement one or more documented access revocation 
programs that collectively include each of the applicable requirements. 
R5 Part 5.4 For termination actions, change 
passwords for shared account(s) known to the 
user within 30 calendar days of the 
termination action. For reassignments or 
transfers, change passwords for shared 
account(s) known to the user within 30 
calendar days following the date that the 
Responsible Entity determines that the 
individual no longer requires retention of that 
access. 
If the Responsible Entity determines and 
documents that extenuating operating 
circumstances require a longer time 
period, change the password(s) within 10 
calendar days following the end of the 
operating circumstances.
